title: KPI Autopilot — Launch Timetable & Readiness Playlist
content:
Purpose:
- Lightweight, operational sheet to drive go/no-go decisions for feature launches that affect inference throughput or cost.
- Combine a short timeline, explicit KPI definitions, thresholded go/no-go signals, and a compact readiness checklist that product-ops can run in the 72h lead-up.

Scope / When to use:
- Use for staged and wide launches where downstream infra or pricing changes could materially affect latency or unit-cost (hosted + dedicated).
- Not for small UI tweaks or purely client-side rollouts.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- KPI Autopilot provides a rolling 10d hygiene window: three preflight checkpoints (T-10, T-3, T-0) + post-launch 72h burn watch.

Owners & escalation:
- Primary: Samira Chen (product-ops) — go/no-go owner.
- Infra SRE: Jon Peters — capacity/OSS kernel impact.
- Serving runtime lead: Maya Singh — model/quantization risk.
- CS/Support lead: Ethan Lopez — customer communications & incident runbook.
-Escalation: PagerDuty channel PD-PROD-LAUNCH, exec alert to VP-Product if RED persists > 30m.

Milestone timetable (compact):
- T-10: Finalize KPI baseline and experiment cohort. Deliverable: baseline report + canary target. Owner: product-ops.
- T-7: Load test + cost simulation (2x expected peak). Deliverable: perf matrix (latency p50/p95), unit-cost delta. Owner: infra SRE.
- T-3: Dry-run with 1% traffic (feature flag). Deliverable: 1% telemetry + sanity checks. Owner: serving lead.
- T-1: Stakeholder sync + rollback plan signoff. Deliverable: signed checklist. Owner: product-ops + CS.
- T+0..T+3: Gradual rollout phases (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with hold points at each step.

KPI definitions & measurement windows (canonical):
- Latency p50 / p95 (ms): measured at the route level (generation endpoint) over 1h windows.
  - Formula: compute aggregated client-side and server-side traces; canonical source: telemetry-api/route-metrics.
- Unit token cost ($/1k tokens): billing-derived rolling 24h. Compare to baseline 7d average.
  - Note: factor in batching efficiency (effective tokens / GPU-hours).
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) as % of requests: 1h rolling.
- KV cache hit ratio (%): 24h median.
- Inference queue depth (requests waiting): 5m sliding max.
- Customer-facing SLA signal: % requests meeting p95 target for tiered customers (24h).

Thresholds (go/no-go binary & triage):
- GREEN (proceed):
  - p95 latency <= baseline * 1.15 AND error rate < 0.5% AND unit token cost delta <= +10%
- YELLOW (hold + investigate):
  - p95 latency between 1.15x and 1.4x baseline OR error rate between 0.5% and 2% OR cost delta between +10% and +25%
  - Actions: pause rollout, mobilize SRE + serving runtime, run targeted load test on canary.
- RED (rollback / abort):
  - p95 latency > baseline * 1.4 OR error rate > 2% OR unit token cost delta > +25% OR queue depth > safe threshold
  - Actions: immediate rollback to last safe release, open Sev1, notify execs and affected customers.

Readiness checklist (T-1 signoff items):
- [ ] Baseline report attached and approved (link + owner).
- [ ] Load test results for 2x peak attached; known regressions documented.
- [ ] Rollback artifact/version pinned in routing layer.
- [ ] Canary health dashboard (latency, errors, cost) created + owners assigned.
- [ ] Incident runbook updated with specific run steps for this launch.
- [ ] CS messaging draft ready (templates for top 5 customers).
- [ ] Autoscaling policies validated for target model variants.
- [ ] Feature flags and kill-switch tested.
- [ ] Security and privacy checklist (PII/noise) verified for model/data path.

Contingency playbook (short):
- If YELLOW: Pause progression, run targeted 30m synthetic test against canary, collect KV cache metrics. If root cause is cache cold-starts, warm KV and remeasure; if cost increase due to dequantization, revert quantization profile.
- If RED: Trigger rollback, notify on-call engineers, post-mortem window scheduled within 72h, customer outreach initiated for impacted accounts.

Post-launch 72h burn watch (T+0..T+3):
- Continuous telemetry collection at 5m granularity for latency, errors, queue depth.
- Daily adoption & usage snapshot at 24h intervals: throughput, unique customer hits, cost delta.
- Hand-off to runbook owner (SRE) at T+3 if stable for 24h.

Quick capacity & cost sanity formulas (for fast checks):
- Estimated GPU-hours per 1M tokens = (avg_tokens_per_request * requests_per_hour * 1M) / (tokens_per_gpu_hour)
  - tokens_per_gpu_hour: derived from kernel profile (appendix in infra-runbooks).
- Unit token cost delta (%) = (new_unit_cost - baseline_unit_cost) / baseline_unit_cost * 100

Monitoring endpoints / dashboards to configure: (examples)
- /dashboards/launches/{launch-id}/latency (p50/p95 heatmap)
- /dashboards/launches/{launch-id}/cost (unit-cost trend, batching efficiency)
- Slack channel: #launch-{launch-id}-ops (automated alerts piped from Prometheus -> PagerDuty -> Slack)
- Alerts: p95 breach (5m sustained), error_rate spike (>1% sustained 15m), queue_depth > threshold

Unresolved questions / notes-to-self:
- Confirm whether Dedicated customers should have separate baseline weighting for p95 (they have stricter SLOs). TODO: ask Maya.
- Need automation to compute effective batching uplift in the sim harness (manual today). TODO: Jon to prototype.
- Consider a short <1h synthetic that simulates typical customer prompt mix rather than uniform tokens — better signal for real-world p95.

Immediate next actions (today):
- Samira: publish baseline report draft to Confluence and ping owners (ETA EOD).
- Jon: run 2x peak perf sim in staging and attach CSV to this doc (ETA +48h).
- Maya: smoke test feature flags and confirm rollback works with canary routing (ETA +24h).

Appendix (signals cheat sheet):
- Small anomalies often from KV cache regeneration: look at cache-miss ratio and cold-start latencies.
- Cost blips often correlate with batch inefficiency after model changes. Check effective batch size metrics.
- If infra kernel upgrade is scheduled in the window, consider delaying launch by 72h.
